items.stem: A team is deciding how to approach work in the 'Account and access administration' area for Snowflake. Which choice best reflects sound practice taught in this module?

options.text: Match the approach to the stated requirement and constraints before choosing a tool
options.rationale: Correct: the module teaches requirement-driven selection rather than defaulting to a favourite tool.

options.text: Always pick the largest or most powerful option available
options.rationale: Over-provisioning raises cost and complexity without addressing the actual requirement.

options.text: Copy a previous project's design without reviewing the new context
options.rationale: Reusing a design blindly ignores differing constraints and is a common error the module warns against.

options.text: Defer the decision until after implementation
options.rationale: Deferring the design decision leads to rework; the module teaches deciding against explicit criteria up front.

items.explanation: Correct: requirement- and constraint-driven selection is the core practice this module establishes.

items.stem: Within 'Performance and cost management', which statement describes the most reliable way to validate the result of the work?

options.text: Confirm the outcome against the defined success criteria and independent checks
options.rationale: Correct: validation against explicit criteria and independent checks is what the module teaches.

options.text: Trust the first output because the tool reported success
options.rationale: A success status does not confirm the result is correct for the requirement.

options.text: Validate only on the data used to build the solution
options.rationale: Checking only on build-time data hides problems that appear on new inputs.
Skipping validation is the failure mode this module is designed to prevent.

items.explanation: Correct: validate against defined criteria with independent checks.

items.stem: Which TWO practices are emphasised in the 'Account and access administration' module of this course? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Design to the requirement and documented constraints
options.rationale: Correct: requirement- and constraint-driven design is a core practice in this module.

options.text: Build in validation or review of the outcome
options.rationale: Correct: validating the outcome against criteria is emphasised throughout the module.

options.text: Prefer the most expensive option by default
options.rationale: Defaulting to the costliest option ignores requirements and raises cost needlessly.
Undocumented decisions undermine review and reproducibility, which the module stresses.

options.text: Treat tool success messages as proof of correctness
options.rationale: A success message is not evidence the result meets the requirement.

items.explanation: Correct: the module emphasises requirement-driven design and built-in validation of the outcome.
